title: Token-priority Orchestrator for Latency-Throughput Tradeoffs in Prefill/Decode
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Design and implement a Token-priority Orchestrator that dynamically balances latency and throughput for prefill/decode workloads. The orchestrator assigns per-request token-priority buckets derived from SLA, observed sequence length, model kernel-cost estimate, and attention cost heuristics. It then coordinates phase splitting or coalescing decisions to meet latency SLOs while maximizing overall throughput and preserving fairness across customers.

Goals:
- Reduce 99th percentile tail latency for latency-sensitive requests (P0/P1 buckets) by up to 25% relative to baseline hybrid arbiter, without regressing overall throughput by more than 10%.
- Ensure starvation protection for low-priority background requests via deficit-style fairness accounting.
- Integrate with kernel selection signals so that heavy-attention phases are scheduled onto kernels/hardware optimized for attention compute, minimizing cross-kernel stalls.
- Provide metrics and rollout knobs in Console: per-bucket latency, token-cost, missed-SLOs, and fairness deltas.

Design notes / approach:
1) Token-priority buckets: compute a continuous priority score for each request at enqueue time using: customer SLA weight, expected remaining tokens (from length predictor), model variant weight (kernel cost table), and recent error-rate penalty. Map score to discrete buckets: P0 (latency-critical), P1 (interactive), P2 (best-effort), P3 (background).
2) Phase-splitting heuristic: when a prefill will exceed a bucket threshold or has mixed attention cost across token ranges, the orchestrator may split the prefill into micro-phases for early decode progress. Splits are bounded by max-splits and minimum slice size to avoid overhead.
3) Opportunistic coalescing: the orchestrator monitors adjacent micro-phases in the queue; if resource and kernel affinity allow, it coalesces to improve batching efficiency for throughput without violating P0 deadlines.
4) Kernel-aware routing: the scheduler uses a kernel cost estimator (offline profiled table + runtime probe signal) to route heavy-attention slices to attention-optimized kernels and lightweight slices to faster low-latency kernels.
5) Fairness & starvation guards: implement a weighted deficit round-robin across customers and buckets with aging to prevent indefinite deferral of P2/P3. Token credit accrual is capped and decays slowly to prevent bursts consuming long-term credits.
6) Safety and fallbacks: if the orchestrator detects sustained missed SLOs for P0, automatically tighten split thresholds and fallback to strict latency-first routing for the affected tenant/route.

Acceptance criteria (tests):
- Bench microbench with synthetic mixes: 20% P0 short (<=32 tokens), 50% P1 medium (128-512 tokens), 30% P2 long (>1024 tokens). Verify 99p latency improvement for P0 and <=10% throughput regression across mixes.
- Fairness test injecting a noisy tenant that continuously issues long P3 requests; validate that other tenants' P2 requests maintain bounded latency and credits.
- Kernel routing correctness: unit tests demonstrating slices with attention-score>0.7 are routed to attention-optimized kernels and callbacks show expected kernel id.
- Integration test across Dedicated and Private deployments ensuring no policy leakage and matching metrics in Console.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: Feature flag behind runtime-schedulers/opt-in. Run A/B on a small fraction of production (5%) with synthetic traffic to validate metrics.
- Stage 2: Increase to 25% after 48h stable. Collect Console dashboards and perf profiles.
- Stage 3: Full rollout for routes that opt in; provide fallback toggle per-customer.

Open risks and trade-offs:
- Splitting increases overhead; tune max-splits and slice sizes to balance overhead vs latency.
- Kernel affinity may reduce batching opportunities; opportunistic coalescing mitigates but requires careful probes to avoid misrouting.
- Complexity could make debugging harder; add tracing points (slice_id, kernel_probe) and structured spans for Console trace view.

Related artifacts: design doc, benchmark results, and prototype PRs listed below.
